name: (none)
role: Not yet given a real state - `class_counter` (`+0x2E`) only increments "for every unit whose state is not 0" (see the unit record), consistent with 0 meaning "just allocated, not yet dispatched" rather than an ordinary idle state. Also doubles as the dispatch convention's own "no transition this tick" sentinel: every per-turn case below returns a next-state byte, and the shared caller only runs the actual state-transition pair when that byte is nonzero - so a case "returning 0" just means "stay put", not literally jumping to state 0. **`+0xC` bit `0x40000000`, generalized this session**: appears throughout this catalog (states 19/26/32/34/36/37/38/39/41/42/43 and others) as a mysterious "pose-variant"/"water-sink" bit tested at the top of a sub-state handler - tracing ~180 of its SETTER sites (not just the test sites) resolves it: it is NOT state- or water-specific at all. It is the generic "my own `+0x2D` SUB-STATE field was just (re)assigned" marker, set in lockstep with every `mov [unit+0x2D],N` across the whole exe - both by `order_execute`'s own 31 order-kind handlers (which reuse `+0x2D` as their OWN internal step counter while a person is in state 10) and by every person-state handler's own internal sub-state machine. A sub-state handler testing this bit at entry is simply asking "was I just switched into this sub-state this tick (need one-time setup) or am I continuing it (skip setup, just tick down)" - completely generic, reused by whichever system currently owns the unit's `+0x2D` field. The "save/exit old state" step of the person-STATE transition pair itself (`0x4ED6F0`, see functions.tsv's own row) is a confirmed no-op and does NOT set this bit - it is set by the higher-level order/sub-state-assigning code instead, orthogonal to `+0x2C` state transitions.

name: tumbling / ground recovery
role: NOT the airborne ballistic flight itself (no velocity/height field +0x49/+0x4B/+0x4D/+0x41 is read anywhere in this function - that physics runs in the separate universal per-unit step, 0x4E6D1D/0x4E6D6D) - this is the GROUND recovery choreography that follows it, confirmed live (a tribe-1 brave hit by Blast enters this state the instant BLOWN, +0xC bit 0x80000, is set). Own sub-state (+0x2D) is a 0/1/2 arrival check (48-unit then 216-unit thresholds against a reference position, meaning unconfirmed) feeding an 8-way jump table (sub-states 3-10): picks a clear nearby cell via an 8-direction offset table (0x895ED9, default 0x895EF1) and moves there (0x4E9DD0); waits randomized timers (+0x70, 4-31 turns, LCG 0x89D178). **The "is this candidate spot OK" check, 0x4D5420, is now traced and confirmed NOT building-aware**: it walks the cell's own linked list (0x8A03E4) filtering strictly for class-1 (person) entries, checking only per-type terrain-climbability (WALK_ALT_DIFF2, movement-profile table 0x5A7B90+0x10, same field state 33 uses) and collision with another live person already claiming the same spot - a building (class 2) on that cell is simply invisible to this check. The sibling function in the initial arrival dispatch, 0x4D5120, is more involved and surfaces one new unconfirmed lead: a per-CELL linked-list HEADER flag (`[cell_list_head+0x1]` bit 0x2, not a per-object field) that, when set, triggers a re-place via 0x4044B0 - plausibly "this cell holds something solid" (a building footprint is the obvious guess, not confirmed). **Resolved, same session, by tracing the physics/landing step itself (0x4E6D00/ground() 0x44E940, see functions.tsv's own rows)**: landing on a building gets no special handling at all - ground() is a pure terrain-height interpolation with no building/class check, so a thrown person always lands at raw terrain height on that cell regardless of any building there; there just isn't a building-awareness mechanism anywhere in this whole chain. **Correction: +0x78 is NOT a trailing-effect counter (an earlier pass of this row wrongly equated it with state 26's own +0xA4 counter) - the Reference already documents +0x78 as a person's plain CARRIED WOOD amount.** The two checks on it here (threshold <1) just pick the matching Idle/Walk vs. holding-wood/Walk-with-wood pose pair (see animation note below); separately, once the first wait timer expires with wood still carried, it spawns a class-5 type-0xB debris effect once per exactly 100 wood decremented from +0x78 (one standard wood load) until 0 - reads as dropping/spilling carried wood in a puff per load while settling, not a generic effect burst (the same +0x78-by-100 pattern also appears in state 41, own row, and in "Preacher conversion"'s sub-state 4 - the same wood-drop mechanic in all three places). NOT ACTUALLY OBSERVED LIVE: the one live trial never logged +0x78/wood, so whether this branch (holding-wood pose, wood-drop puffs) fired for that specific brave is unknown - needs a wood-carrying brave specifically. Every 32 turns while grounded, two more LCG rolls can kick it back into sub-state 6 (~13/32) or 10 (~3/64), both also setting flags+0xC bit 0x40000000 (the same bit cheat.md's live drowning trace found on entering the water-sink sequence, and state 37, own row, toggles repeatedly - looks like a general pose-variant bit, not confirmed water-exclusive) - this randomness is why live substates wander non-monotonically (4→5→10→5→6→7…) instead of counting through a fixed sequence. Sub-state 7 ("getting up") rerolls a fresh facing/timer before looping back. Exit: two epilogues return the per-type default state via the same table 0x5A7064 state 1 (0x4D3386) uses, one a fixed state 0x27 (39, shaman debug-mode override, same pattern as 0x518560). **Cross-system note, traced this session**: this state's own entry trigger (BLOWN, `+0xC` bit `0x80000`, set) and the in-FIGHT stagger/push (person_states state 25's stance 7, `fight_turn`/`0x518FB0`'s own row) are the SAME physics mechanism - a fight-stagger sets this exact bit too, and `fight_turn`'s own "has this fighter landed yet" check (`+0xE` bit `0x8`) is byte-aligned shorthand for this same `+0xC` bit `0x80000` DWORD, not a separate flag. So "waking up" from a fight knockback is the in-combat counterpart to this state's own "wait for BLOWN to clear, then recover" trigger - same signal, different owner (the fight controller's own stance field vs. this person state). Ghidra's function range for 0x4D73E0 (claimed end 0x4D80B9) is wrong - 0x4D7FD0 inside that range is actually the death/spirit-rise record push (state 3's own mechanism), a separate function. **Animations resolved this session, directly from the exe's static data (0x5A6D50/0x5A6858, "Fight"'s own `[action×9+type]` table at 0x4D3FF0, cross-checked against 7 already-known action values, all matching)**: no dedicated "down" sprite - calls 0x4D3FF0 with actions 1/5 (already-documented Walk/Walk-with-wood, picked by the +0x78 wood check above) while moving to the picked spot, and 0/4 while settling, resolving to plain Idle (action 0, VSTART 6/53) and VSTART 10 ("standing still, holding wood", brave-specific, action 4, likewise wood-gated) - both already named in open-populous animations.md. So this whole recovery window most likely looks like an ordinary idle/standing (or holding-wood, if carrying any) person that just isn't taking orders, plus a few dropped-wood puffs if it had wood - not a visibly prolonged "struggling on the ground" animation. This static table-reading is independently cross-checked against 7 already-known action values (all matched exactly) but NOT itself confirmed against this specific live trial. See open-populous pop3-rev-analysis.md "Tumbling and ground recovery" / "A blasted person fighting back".

handler: 0x4D3832 (per-turn), 0x4D2D74 (entry, in `init_unit_class_1`/0x4D2740's own per-state ENTER dispatch, `switchD_004d290b` caseD_1a)

"screaming" in the old claim is unconfirmed/likely wrong. **Gating, confirmed by direct comparison**: entry via the blast-push code (`0x50B740`, `test BYTE PTR [+0x7A],0x1`) only fires this for a pushed person when the BLAST INSTANCE's own `+0x7A` bit 0x1 is set - i.e. **Firestorm's blast genuinely does force this run on its victims; Lightning's own companion blast genuinely does not**, a real difference, not a trace gap. Entry via the burning-building eviction path (`0x408AB0`/`0x408B39`) is UNCONDITIONAL (that path sets the state directly via the standard `0x4ED6F0`/`0x4ED640` state-transition pair, never passing through `0x50B740`'s own `+0x7A` gate at all) - every evicted occupant gets the forced run, matching open-populous's existing "Burning building" trace's "and panics" wording exactly as originally written. **Insect plague's own building raid (`0x510120`, functions.tsv) uses the exact same unconditional path; its own direct 3x3-cell "sting" (every 8 turns) uses a THIRD, independent gate - the victim's own +0xE bit 0x10 - and applies `SWARM_PERSON_DAMAGE` (100) via `0x4DA080` right after, see functions.tsv's `0x510120` row.** Not re-checked this session: whether Blast's own spell-cast blast (as opposed to Firestorm/Volcano's fireball-created one) sets `+0x7A` too.

name: Angel of Death hunting AI
role: The angel's entire lifetime runs through this one state (table 0x4D3D18 index 27; also called directly once, synchronously, right at spawn from `0x4DD700`/`create_aod`) - the only type-8 (angel) state, confirmed via the per-type default-fallback table 0x5A7064 (only type 8 maps here). Outer dispatch on `+0x2D`: cases 0,1,3,4,6,7,8,0xA,0xB (nested),0xF,0x10 exist (per `backup.xml`'s own `switchD_`/`caseD_` symbols at this function's own switch address) but are not yet opened; anything else falls to a shared tail. Case 5, the dominant "hunting/engaged" case, is the part now fully read: target acquisition checks for a nearby ENEMY type-8 angel first (confirmed for both acquisition and in-combat priority - see below), else falls back to the same per-tribe-table scan ordinary combat uses, reusing combat's own attacker/candidate type-pairing rule (`0x51C4C0`'s rule, independently duplicated here: self type 8 accepts ANY candidate type, including type 7/shaman, confirming the angel can target shamans) and explicitly skipping any candidate in state 23 (the preacher-conversion roll, same exclusion `0x51D0B0` uses). A locked target is kept in `+0x72` (distinct from `+0x89`, see below). Against a non-angel locked target: an engagement-roll sub-state (`+0xA8`==0, via `0x4DADA0`, a 1-in-64 roar) arms an alert flag (`+0x76` bit 0x10), checks whether the target is housed inside a tower (via the target's own cell's class-2/type-4 building link) to pick a wider standoff distance (200 units) than an open target (160), waits two ticks, then (`+0xA8`==1) either closes in to grab the target or, if the locked target is ITSELF a type-8 angel, switches to health-compared mutual damage (`0x4E0830`) at a tighter range (312 units) instead of grabbing - "two angels fight by health." Grabbing a non-angel victim: writes the angel's own id into the victim's `+0x72` ("who is holding me," unless already claimed by another angel), forces the victim into **person state 40** (see that row), and doubles the angel's own flight speed. `+0xA8`==2 runs a fixed 28-turn carry (self `+0x70` = 0x1C, matching "about one kill per 28 turns/2.3s" exactly): climbs +800 height units, slows, zigzags heading +-22/2048 radians per tick. At countdown 8, `0x4E0A30` sets a throw destination 400 units along the VICTIM's OWN current facing (not the angel's), arms the victim's own drop (`+0x2D`=1), charges the angel a self-damage cost (gated on an unresolved condition - plausibly per-kill wear on its own `LIFE_AOD` pool, not confirmed), then calls the generic "finalize landing/settled position" helper (`0x4D3EA0`, functions.tsv's own row - the same one ordinary touchdown/tumbling-recovery use) on the victim. At countdown 7: a 180-degree wind-up turn, reposition, and another roar.
